root.name: Article on Lilith
root.description: Article by Jane Doe published in 2019 at https://example.org/lilith presenting Lilith as a female demon of Jewish tradition originating from a Mesopotamian deity, and describing her in medieval Jewish legends (specifically the Alphabet of Ben Sira) as Adam's first wife before Eve.

children.name: Publication details
children.description: The source is an article titled 'Article on Lilith' written by Jane Doe, published in 2019, accessible at URL https://example.org/lilith.

children.name: Lilith's nature and origin
children.description: Lilith is defined as a female demon in Jewish tradition who stands for a deity of Mesopotamian origin.

children.name: Role in Jewish tradition
children.description: In Jewish tradition, Lilith is characterized as a female demon.

children.name: Mesopotamian deity origin
children.description: Lilith represents a deity that originated in Mesopotamia.

children.name: Lilith in medieval Jewish legends
children.description: In the Jewish legends that spread during the Middle Ages, according to the Alphabet of Ben Sira, Lilith is presented as Adam's first wife, preceding Eve.

children.name: Alphabet of Ben Sira
children.description: The Alphabet of Ben Sira is the textual source within medieval Jewish legends that presents Lilith as Adam's first wife.

children.name: Adam's first wife before Eve
children.description: According to medieval Jewish legends, Lilith was Adam's first wife, existing before Eve.
